names.name: Samantabhadra (Kun tu bzang po), the dharmakāya primordial buddha
the nature of the sugatas (bde gshegs snying po)
great purity and equality (dag mnyam chen po)

descriptions: All phenomena are primordially buddha: 'from the unborn all is born; in being born there is no birth' (Guhyagarbha ch.2).
Appearances are primordially pure as the maṇḍala of deities (the aggregates are the five buddhas, Guhyagarbha ch.1) and equal in emptiness.
In Mipham's Nyingma reading, buddha-nature is the union of luminosity and emptiness, with the qualities spontaneously present.
negations: no arising, abiding, ceasing, coming or going (Guhyagarbha ch.2)
no bondage and no liberation: 'no one binds, there is no bondage' (Guhyagarbha ch.2)
relation_to_self: Beings are primordially buddhas whose own conceptual grasping at 'I' and 'mine' ties 'knots in space'; the 'self' is not established, but the nature of mind is the sugatagarbha.
relation_to_world: The world as it appears through karmic delusion is the five realms; as it is, it is the spontaneously present maṇḍala (pure appearance).
caveat: The Nyingma deny a creator god and a permanent self: Samantabhadra is the dharmakāya — the ground recognized — not a person who made the world, and the sugatagarbha is not the self of the tīrthikas (Mipham). The one-truth reading is acceptable only as 'one ground, two paths' (recognition and non-recognition), not as the identity of all doctrines.

names.name: the ground (gzhi): primordial purity and spontaneous presence
bodhicitta, the all-creating king (byang chub kyi sems kun byed rgyal po)

descriptions: Essence empty (ngo bo stong pa), nature luminous (rang bzhin gsal ba), compassion all-pervading (thugs rje kun khyab) — the three aspects of the ground.
Primordially pure (ka dag) and spontaneously present (lhun grub).
'I am primordially self-arising wisdom, the essence of all phenomena' (Kunjed Gyalpo ch.4); the variety is non-dual, free of elaboration in its parts (Kunjed Gyalpo ch.31).
negations: not made, not to be sought, not attained by meditation (Kunjed Gyalpo ch.45)
beyond view, meditation, samaya, grounds and paths to traverse (Kunjed Gyalpo ch.44)
neither existent nor non-existent, free of the extremes (Longchenpa)
relation_to_self: Awareness is one's own nature; recognizing it is buddhahood, not recognizing it is the beginning of saṃsāra (one ground, two paths).
relation_to_world: Appearances arise as the ground's own display (rtsal, rol pa); deluded beings take them as external objects; in realization they self-liberate.
caveat: The 'all-creating king' of the Kunjed Gyalpo is awareness itself speaking, not a creator distinct from beings; Dzogchen also distinguishes the ground from the all-base (kun gzhi) and awareness from mind (sems), and would reject any identification of rig pa with a merely thoughtless state or with a Brahman-like self.

names.name: Kuntu Zangpo, the primordial buddha of Bön
bon nyid (the reality of Bön) and bon sku (the Bön-body)

descriptions: The base (kun gzhi) is empty and clear, and awareness (rig pa) is inseparable from it; their union is called 'mother and son' (ma bu) in the Zhang Zhung Nyengyü (moderate confidence).
Kuntu Zangpo is the Bön-body; Shenlha Ökar the body of perfection; Tönpa Shenrab the emanation body.
negations: the base is not a thing established by characteristics; awareness cannot be grasped as an object
relation_to_self: The nature of one's own mind (sems nyid) is the base; recognizing it is Buddhahood.
relation_to_world: Appearances arise from the base as light, sound and rays; not recognizing them as the base's own display is the origin of saṃsāra.
caveat: Bön insists on its own origin (Tönpa Shenrab, Tagzig) and would reject being read as a variant of Buddhism; its 'kun gzhi' is the ultimate base, whereas in Nyingma usage 'kun gzhi' (all-base) usually names the ground of saṃsāric consciousness — the same word is not the same doctrine.
notes: Optional (Bön). Built from general knowledge; confidence low-moderate.
